function: Joint learned AP clustering (PPO at edge cloud) and per-AP downlink power allocation (MAPPO) for UAV multi-connectivity under finite-blocklength reliability and minimum total power (p. 7-8)
system: Downlink: 19 ground APs at 25 m with 16-antenna arrays serve 6 single-antenna UAVs; no RIS; 2.0 GHz carrier, 10 MHz bandwidth (p. 3, 9)
method: Hierarchical multi-agent RL: PPO for clustering at the edge cloud, MAPPO for power at the APs, action-observation transition; trained offline in a digital twin (p. 8)
data_channel: 3GPP TR 36.777 path loss, LoS/NLoS and fading [29], Rayleigh outage formula, stochastic 3D UAV mobility, 3 km square area; no dataset (p. 4, 5, 9)
test_conditions: Trained offline in a digital twin; one evaluation setup (6 UAVs, 19 APs); DEP threshold swept; 16 to 32 APs only for training time (p. 8, 9, 12)
baselines: Learned: MSAC [1] (authors' earlier centralized method) and non-hierarchical MAPPO. Non-learned: JCPC optimization [8], opportunistic clustering [16], closest AP (p. 9)
metrics: DEP threshold violations, SINR outage CDF, total transmit power, cluster size, cluster reconfiguration rate, training reward, episode time (p. 10-13)
complexity: Table IV: per-step complexity O(KLH^2 + NKH) and 4-8 ms runtime per step for the proposed method; episode time versus number of APs (p. 11-12)
q1_support: p. 4: "These effects are modeled according to the 3GPP specifications for AUs [29]" (TR 36.777, Enhanced LTE Support for Aerial Vehicles); p. 9: "path-loss follows [29]"; another standardized model, reviewer to confirm it is more than path loss.
q2_support: p. 9: "They are served by K = 19 APs," with N = 6 users is the only evaluation setup; p. 13: Fig. 7 "relative time needed to complete an episode" varies APs for training time only; no unseen scenario tested.
q3_support: p. 9: "MSAC: A centralized off-policy approach called masked" soft actor-critic from [1], earlier learned method of the same authors; p. 9: "scheme proposed in [8], employs iterative algorithms" (JCPC, non-learned); p. 11: "achieves the DEP threshold with the lowest transmit power."
q4_support: p. 10: "as summarized in Table IV, H-MAPPO benefits from parallel"; Table IV (p. 11) lists per-step complexity O(KLH^2 + NKH) and runtime 4-8 ms for the proposed H-MAPPO.
q5_support: p. 9: "publicly available with the final version of the paper." is only a promise of the source code, with no link or DOI; custom Gym simulator, no public channel dataset.
notes: Borderline eligibility: the learned decisions are AP clustering for UAV mobility management (user association, above the physical layer) and per-AP power allocation (physical layer) taken jointly; included under the rule that a learned physical-layer decision in an aerial link learned jointly with one above it passes above_phy, area 6 as power control for UAV links; reviewer should confirm. q1 is met on the 3GPP TR 36.777 aerial model [29], a standardized model other than TR 38.901 or TR 38.811; p. 4 says path loss and fading follow it, but p. 9 says only the path loss follows it and p. 5 derives the outage with Rayleigh fading. The MAPPO baseline is a non-hierarchical variant, so q3 rests on MSAC [1] and JCPC [8]. The abstract calls the 10 percent versus 90 percent result decision time, while p. 12 and the Fig. 7 caption call it training time per episode. Tables I to IV were read from the page images.
